purpose: Versioned qualification backlog for real manufacturing interoperability targets; distinguishes published standard scope, candidate payloads, required evidence, benchmark targets and implemented capability.

targets.role: Computer-checkable message syntax, semantic encoding, and conformance to a characteristic-data specification. ISO's published scope explicitly excludes provenance, accuracy and completeness assertions, which are addressed by separate parts.
targets.candidate_payload_family: Characteristic-data messages with explicit data-specification identity and version.
required_inputs: Authoritative specification version and lawful access to normative content
Machine-readable syntax/data specification and independent validator version
Positive and negative conformance messages
Reviewed mappings for unit, property identifier, scope and source revision
A scope decision identifying whether the project also needs ISO 8000-120 provenance, ISO 8000-130 accuracy, or ISO 8000-140 completeness assertions

benchmarks.acceptance: Every committed positive/negative message agrees with the pinned independent validator; source/spec versions and digests are recorded.
Every inventory field is preserved, explicitly transformed, explicitly dropped with reviewed reason, or listed as unmapped; absent optional fields still count.
A construct outside the implemented and declared profile blocks qualification rather than being approximated.

targets.role: Requirements and a data model for capturing and exchanging information about the provenance/pedigree of characteristic property values; supplements ISO 8000-110 and does not itself specify an exchange format.
targets.candidate_payload_family: Provenance statements about property values, source/derivation references and the named data specification; mapped to the OMSI derivation graph only under a reviewed profile.
required_inputs: Authoritative ISO 8000-120:2016 edition and normative requirements
Reviewed provenance terms and mapping from property-value pedigree to OMSI entities/activities
Positive and negative fixtures for missing, conflicting and mutated provenance
A policy separating provenance assertions from source authentication and measurement truth

benchmarks.acceptance: Every required provenance element for the pinned use case is preserved or explicitly reported missing; no value is labeled proven solely because provenance fields exist.
Every fixture reconstructs the expected source/derivation chain with exact artifact references and versioned activity semantics.
Mutated digests, broken links and contradictory source/derived claims are detected and surfaced.

targets.role: Requirements and a conceptual model for representing/exchanging statements or assertions about characteristic-data accuracy; it does not define a universal accuracy requirement or measurement method.
targets.candidate_payload_family: Typed accuracy assertions with source, scope, method/reference, applicable population and evidence links; do not turn them into a universal numeric accuracy score.
required_inputs: Authoritative ISO 8000-130:2016 edition and normative model
Explicit semantics for each accuracy assertion and its scope/population
Independent calculation or reference evidence where an assertion is derived
Metrology review to distinguish data accuracy statements from physical measurement uncertainty and calibration

benchmarks.acceptance: Every reported accuracy assertion carries the approved scope and source/evidence references and retains its typed meaning.
No syntax-valid or signed accuracy assertion alone upgrades the OMSI outcome to measurement-proven or quality-released.
A second implementation reproduces every explicitly computed accuracy assertion or flags it as issuer-provided rather than independently calculated.

targets.role: Requirements and a conceptual model for statements/assertions about completeness, optionally supplementing ISO 8000-120; it does not establish universal completeness requirements or specify a complete exchange format.
targets.candidate_payload_family: Completeness assertions bound to a named data specification, population, time/revision and expected field inventory.
required_inputs: Authoritative ISO 8000-140:2016 edition and normative model
Declared completeness expectation per use case and data population
Versioned source schema/inventory and expected versus observed counts
Negative fixtures for omitted optional/required properties and incorrect population boundaries

benchmarks.acceptance: Every completeness assertion refers to a versioned field inventory and population; no count is interpreted without that boundary.
Every required field missing from a sample or a declared population is surfaced according to the profile; optional omissions remain distinguishable.
Expected completeness thresholds are never confused with observed results.

targets.role: Assessment indicators for data-quality management processes; not a source-record wire format.
targets.candidate_payload_family: Versioned evidence for a data-quality indicator definition, population, calculation and result.
required_inputs: Indicator definition/version and assessment boundary
Data-processing work products from a representative workflow
Evidence distinguishing observed results from targets/self-reported status
Reviewed aggregation and sampling policy

benchmarks.acceptance: Every indicator result links to definition/version, population, time window, evidence inputs and calculation activity.
Targets and missing measurements remain explicitly labeled; a target is never emitted as an observed pass.
A separate implementation reproduces committed calculation fixtures and detects tampered inputs or calculation metadata.

targets.role: Integrated model for manufacturing quality information, including inspection and measurement information.
targets.candidate_payload_family: Version-pinned QIF XML with the normative schema assets for that version.
required_inputs: Authoritative QIF version and schema bundle
Pinned XML/XSD validator and schema-bundle digests
Representative valid/invalid QIF measurement and inspection fixtures
Reviewed mapping for identifiers, units, specification/revision, uncertainty where represented, and source-versus-derived claims

benchmarks.acceptance: 100% agreement with the pinned independent XSD validator on positive and negative fixtures.
Every source field has exactly one reviewed disposition; no silent loss or unreviewed unit/identifier reinterpretation.
Declared lossless fields survive import/export exactly or under an approved semantic comparison; known-loss fields have explicit tests and disclosure.

targets.role: Defines quality characteristics for streams of single, discrete digital sensor values, anomaly types and their relationships; it does not specify methods to measure or improve data quality.
targets.candidate_payload_family: Version-pinned discrete sensor observations plus typed data-quality characteristics/anomaly labels.
required_inputs: Authoritative ISO 8000-210:2024 edition and characteristic/anomaly definitions
Representative sensor streams including missing, duplicated, stale, out-of-order and anomalous observations
Preserved acquisition timestamps, source identity, units and stream scope
Independent fixture oracle and documented sampling/window policy

benchmarks.acceptance: All committed characteristic/anomaly fixtures match the independent oracle for the pinned profile.
Annotating anomalies does not silently rewrite the original observation bytes or timestamps.
Unknown or unsupported characteristics are retained as unknown and cannot be reported as conformant by default.

targets.role: Specifies quality measures for quantitatively measuring the sensor data quality characteristics defined by ISO 8000-210.
targets.candidate_payload_family: Version-pinned quality measures with named characteristic, calculation method, sample/window population, assumptions and result report.
required_inputs: Authoritative ISO 8000-220:2025 measures and corresponding ISO 8000-210 characteristics
Documented assumptions and sampling/window definitions
Reference fixtures with independently calculated measure results
Controls preventing missing samples or invalid windows being treated as high quality

benchmarks.acceptance: Every pinned measure fixture matches an independent reference calculation within its declared numeric representation.
Identical input bytes, algorithm/profile version and window produce equivalent results and identical provenance metadata.
Missing, insufficient or structurally invalid populations are flagged and never given an optimistic quality result.

targets.role: Guidelines for cleansing sensor-data anomalies and improving data quality; the published scope does not specify detailed anomaly-repair algorithms or real-time cleansing.
targets.candidate_payload_family: Auditable cleansing activity with preserved raw samples, anomaly classification, method/version, repair rationale, outputs and lineage.
required_inputs: Authoritative ISO/TS 8000-230:2026 edition and applicable process guidance
Explicit policy for which anomalies may be corrected, flagged or left unresolved
Raw samples retained separately from cleaned outputs
Validation fixtures measuring false-positive repairs, missed anomalies and impact on downstream decision

benchmarks.acceptance: Every cleaned output retains a reference to the immutable original sample and the named cleansing activity.
A verifier reconstructs input samples, method/version, parameters, changed values and stated reason from the evidence bundle.
No cleanup heuristic silently overwrites a physical observation or upgrades a quality/release outcome.
Both rates are measured against a labeled reference corpus; all performance targets are corpus-specific and disclosed.

targets.standard: MTConnect and OPC UA Companion Specifications (versions pinned per pilot)
targets.role: Device observations and companion information models across machine, server, client and adapter boundaries.
targets.candidate_payload_family: Version-pinned MTConnect observations and OPC UA nodeset/address-space fixtures through a simulator or server/client integration.
required_inputs: Specific MTConnect and OPC UA Companion Specification versions
Authoritative schemas/nodesets and provenance/licensing records
Simulator/server/client test path returning varied device/observation structures
Reviewed identifier, timestamp, unit, asset-scope and source-revision mapping rules

benchmarks.acceptance: Every positive fixture reaches the client/receipt with expected identifiers, scope, times, units and values; malformed and unauthorized cases reject.
Declared lossless fields preserve semantic values across device model, adapter and evidence receipt; intentional loss remains explicit and counted.
Unknown nodes and version mismatches are surfaced; no qualified/conformant state is emitted optimistically.
Two independently provisioned verifier agents agree on artifact/graph and fixture outcomes; agreement is not asserted to prove physical truth.

cross_cutting_gates.acceptance: Each result binds source bytes, schema/spec version and bytes, adapter-map bytes, tool identity/version and output report; digests do not authenticate the producer.
Mutations to unit, identifier, tenant scope, source revision, required presence, schema version, malformed XML/JSON, replay bytes and schema constraints remain negative controls.
Schema validation, field mapping, semantic evaluation, artifact binding and authentication are reported as separate checks; an implementation may not be the sole oracle for its own conformance.

non_claims: No ISO, QIF, MTConnect, OPC UA or vendor conformance is currently asserted.
Synthetic JSON fixtures do not replace normative schema assets or a real device/client-server integration path.
A valid schema instance, mapping audit, hash or signature does not by itself prove producer authenticity or physical measurement truth.
Benchmark targets in this matrix are proposed acceptance objectives, not normative thresholds or measured outcomes.

ISO 8000-120/130/140 cover provenance, accuracy and completeness information models/assertions; their existence does not establish that data is true, accurate, or complete without a defined use-case policy and evidence.

references.id: NIST testing of the MTConnect–OPC UA Companion Specification
